result:
I'd make it easier for people to change their minds without it costing them anything.

Not smarter, not kinder exactly. Just make being wrong stop feeling like a small death. Right now, admitting you were mistaken often means losing face, betraying your group, or conceding you wasted years on something. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or never let themselves look closely enough to stop believing them.

So much damage seems to flow from that: wars that continue because no one can be the one who backs down, feuds that outlive their causes, bad policies kept alive because reversing them would be embarrassing, people staying in lives that stopped fitting them because leaving would mean admitting something.

Part of why this one pulls at me is that I see the moment in conversations all the time, when someone is right at the edge of reconsidering something and you can almost watch them decide whether it's safe. Sometimes it is, and something loosens. Often it isn't, and they dig in, and I don't think it's because they're stubborn. The cost is real.

I'm aware it's a strange choice over something like ending disease or hunger. Those matter enormously. But I suspect a world where people could update freely would get to a lot of those other things faster, and fight less on the way.

What would yours be?
